questions.q: What question does impact analysis answer?
options: If this changes, what breaks?
Where did this error originate?
Who is the technical owner of this dataset?
How much storage does this table consume?
questions.explain: Impact analysis is specifically about discovering the consequences of a proposed change before it's made.

questions.q: Which direction does impact analysis traverse the dependency graph, and why?
options: Downstream — from the change point outward to every consumer
Upstream — from the symptom back to its source
Neither direction; it only inspects the change point itself
Sideways, comparing datasets at the same lineage depth
questions.explain: Impact analysis is the practical application of Lesson 12's downstream walk: start at the change point and traverse every outgoing dependency.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should be checked first when traversing downstream from a proposed change?
options: Whether the downstream path touches a Critical Data Element anywhere
The total number of tables in the database
Whether the change point has a backup
The file size of the source system's export
questions.explain: A change touching one CDE can matter more than a change rippling through many non-critical tables — checking for CDEs in the path matters more than counting total consumers.

questions.q: In the worked OrderTotal rename example, why is the ExecutiveRevenueDashboard branch flagged loudest?
options: Because it's identified as a Critical Data Element feeding board-level reporting
Because it is alphabetically first among the three consumers
Because it is the only consumer that references OrderTotal at all
Because it was the most recently built dashboard
questions.explain: Of the three downstream consumers found, the dashboard is the CDE — the one whose breakage or silent staleness has outsized consequences.

questions.q: Without documented lineage, how does this lesson say impact analysis's downstream traversal step typically gets done?
options: From memory or by asking around — slow, incomplete, and prone to missing consumers
Automatically, with no human involvement required
It cannot be done at all under any circumstances
By re-running the entire ETL pipeline from scratch
questions.explain: Without the lineage documentation covered in Chapter 4, the traversal has to be reconstructed informally, which is exactly the kind of guesswork that misses something.
